decision_reason: Iteration 1 returned strong candidate sources (paho.org ×7, reliefweb.int ×7, who.int ×3, iris.paho.org ×2, gtfcc.org ×2) that are clearly relevant to Haiti cholera 2024. A second iteration should: (a) directly target MSPP's own domain for 2024 bulletins; (b) target PAHO's Haiti-specific situation report series (reports 9–15+ covering mid-to-late 2024); (c) target ReliefWeb with date-filtered queries for 2024 Haiti cholera humanitarian reports; (d) target UNICEF Haiti and MSF as secondary humanitarian actors with field-level data. This is iteration 2 of 2 (max), so the query batch must be maximally targeted.

decision_reason: Two iterations have been completed and the hard limit of max_iterations=2 has been reached. The search has surfaced a strong and diverse set of candidate sources covering the 2024 Haiti cholera task, but three meaningful gaps remain unresolved due to the iteration cap: (1) MSPP direct domain (mspp.gouv.ht) returned zero results across both iterations — the site:mspp.gouv.ht query in iteration 2 produced no accepted candidates from that domain, meaning the primary national surveillance authority's own bulletins are not represented in the candidate pool; (2) PAHO's joint Haiti Humanitarian Situation Reports (post-March 2024, covering Q2–Q4 2024) were referenced in the Situation Report 8 snippet ("Since March 2024, joint reports have been prepared on the humanitarian crisis and the cholera outbreak in Haiti. Check these reports for the latest updates on the cholera situation. Haiti's Humanitarian Situation Reports") but the individual post-March 2024 joint reports were not surfaced as distinct accepted candidates; (3) UNICEF's index page (unicef.org/appeals/haiti/situation-reports) was accepted and its snippet explicitly lists monthly 2024 SitReps (January–February, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November 2024) — these individual documents are high-value candidates but were not individually surfaced. Despite these gaps, the candidate pool is substantively sufficient for the collection workflow to proceed: PAHO Situation Report 8 (March 2024), PAHO April 2024 epidemiological update, PAHO documents index, UNICEF SitRep index with 2024 monthly links, WHO DONs, ReliefWeb, GTFCC, and BEACON are all present. The unexecuted follow-up queries below are documented for transparency but cannot be executed within the current bounds.
coverage_assessment: Temporal coverage: PAHO Situation Report 8 (13 March 2024) and PAHO epidemiological update (26 April 2024) confirm Q1 2024 coverage. The UNICEF SitRep index snippet explicitly lists monthly reports from January–February 2024 through November 2024, providing a near-complete 2024 temporal chain. Post-March 2024 PAHO joint humanitarian/cholera reports are referenced but not individually surfaced. December 2024 is not explicitly confirmed in any accepted candidate. Geographic coverage: National-level Haiti data is well-covered. Subnational (department-level) data is not confirmed in any accepted snippet — MSPP bulletins (the primary subnational source) were not retrieved. Field coverage: cases_suspected, deaths, and date_reported are likely present in PAHO and UNICEF documents. cases_confirmed, hospitalizations, and subnational_location fields remain uncertain without MSPP or individual UNICEF SitRep content.
source_diversity_assessment: Source diversity is good across international organizations (PAHO, WHO, UNICEF, OCHA/ReliefWeb, GTFCC) and secondary aggregators (BEACON, choleraalliance.org). Academic sources (AJTMH, PMC) are present but cover 2022 outbreak investigation, not 2024 surveillance data. The critical missing source type is the national health authority (MSPP) direct publications. News sources (haitiantimes.com) appeared but with garbled date metadata and should be treated with caution. No MSF or IRC field reports were surfaced despite being targeted in iteration 2.
trustworthiness_assessment: High-trust sources dominate the accepted candidate pool: paho.org (5 results), who.int (3), unicef.org (3), reliefweb.int (2), gtfcc.org (1). These are all authoritative international public health or humanitarian organizations. BEACON (beaconbio.org) is a credible academic disease surveillance aggregator (Boston University/HealthMap). The haitiantimes.com result has garbled date references (mixing 2022, 2025 dates in the same snippet) and should be flagged for human review before use as evidence. The MSPP absence is a trust gap — national authority data would be the gold standard for subnational figures.
disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Disease fit: All accepted candidates are explicitly about cholera in Haiti — high relevance. Location fit: Haiti is the primary location in all accepted candidates. Time fit: This is the primary weakness. Most confirmed snippets reference 2022 outbreak data. The PAHO April 2024 epidemiological update and PAHO Situation Report 8 (March 2024) are the only candidates with confirmed 2024 dates in their titles/snippets. The UNICEF SitRep index lists 2024 monthly reports by title, which are strong candidates for 2024 data but their content was not confirmed in snippets. The iteration cap prevents further targeted retrieval of Q3–Q4 2024 specific documents.
corroboration_potential_assessment: Strong corroboration potential exists across three independent source chains: (1) PAHO/WHO official situation reports and epidemiological updates; (2) UNICEF monthly humanitarian situation reports (which cite MSPP data); (3) OCHA/ReliefWeb aggregated humanitarian reports. BEACON (Boston University/HealthMap) provides a secondary aggregation layer. The absence of direct MSPP documents is the primary corroboration gap — UNICEF and PAHO SitReps typically cite MSPP as their primary data source, so MSPP figures are likely embedded in those documents even if the MSPP domain itself was not retrieved.
